Subject: DPA clarifications & next steps for Redwood — Zenith Payments

Hi Tom (and Sofia),

Thanks again for the time earlier — really helpful to walk through Zenith's integration pattern and the compliance hurdles you mentioned. Per our call, I wanted to recap the open DPA/privacy items and propose next steps so we can keep the procurement track moving: 

Open items you flagged:
- Controller vs. Processor: confirm roles for telemetry and logs generated during inference.
- Subprocessors: list of current subprocessors and process for notice/objection.
- Breach notice / incident timelines and what information is provided in event of an incident.
- Data residency & storage: whether logs or KV cache ever leave the selected region.
- PII identification & retention: default retention windows and ability to configure per-customer retention.
- Logging controls: what is captured (prompt, user id, metadata), and options for redaction/pseudonymization.

What I'm attaching: Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf — this is the latest DPA we typically send to customers; it already includes processor/controller language and subprocessor list in Appendix A.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will ask Legal to confirm the standard controller/processor language and the process for providing subprocessor updates (we can provide 30-day notice and an objection right for specific processors).
2) I'll confirm the breach notification SLA (we typically notify within 72 hours of confirming a security incident; we can provide reasonably available detail and live updates).
3) Engineering will run a short technical note on data residency and KV cache placement for your specific region (US-east).
4) If you want any specific changes to retention or logging guarantees, we can discuss addenda or a security profile for the Dedicated offering.

Can you confirm whether you need: (a) a signed DPA before pilot, or (b) the doc as-is to satisfy procurement initially and signature during contract stage? Also let me know if there are any other folks on your side who should be looped in.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the DPA. A few clarifying questions from legal and engineering after a quick pass: 

1) Controller/Processor: Our legal team needs explicit confirmation that Zenith will be the controller for customer data (i.e., prompts and customer-provided data) and that Redwood will act as a processor for hosted inference. Section 2 of your DPA is a bit generic — can you point us to the exact clause or provide a one-paragraph statement we can share with our counsel?

2) Subprocessors: Please confirm the current list of subprocessors and the notice period for new subprocessors. Also whether we have an objection right (on reasonable grounds) and what happens if we object.

3) Breach notice: We require initial notification within 48 hours of detection, and a follow-up with likely impact and remediation steps within 5 business days. Is Redwood able to commit to these timelines or provide a rationale if not?

4) Data residency & KV cache: Our engineers are concerned about KV cache or temporary logs leaving the us-east region during model inference or when fallbacks occur to other model variants. Can you confirm how cache and temp logs are routed?

5) Retention & logging: We need the ability to shorten retention of prompts/outputs to 30 days for the pilot; can we set that via account settings or do we need a contract addendum? Also any controls for redacting PII at ingestion or masking tokens post-hoc?

Would appreciate a one-page written response we can share with counsel/engineering. If easier, happy to take a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Cloud Security
Zenith Payments

Tom — thanks, great questions. I pulled answers together below and looped in Dev from our security/engineering team for the technical bits. Where appropriate I marked the DPA section references and noted what we can do via configuration vs. contract.

1) Controller/Processor (DPA §1.1–1.3): Redwood's standard stance for hosted API customers is that the customer (Zenith) is the Controller of customer-provided content (prompts, customer data) and Redwood is the Processor. We will provide a short paragraph you can paste to counsel: 

"Zenith Payments is the Controller of Customer Data submitted to the Redwood service. Redwood Inference acts as Processor and processes Customer Data only on behalf of and under the documented instructions of Zenith Payments in accordance with the DPA."

2) Subprocessors (Appendix A): Current subprocessors are listed in Appendix A of the attached DPA (cloud infra provider, monitoring provider, analytics). We provide 30 days' notice before adding a new subprocessor and maintain a documented objection process; if you object on reasonable grounds we will discuss alternatives (e.g., use of a different provider for that function or contractual mitigations). We can add an express objection right clause if required.

3) Breach notice (DPA §5): Our standard notification window is initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident. I understand Zenith's preference for 48 hours — I flagged this with Security. Dev, can you confirm whether we can tighten to 48 hours for this account / pilot, or provide an escalation procedure that meets their needs?

4) Data residency & KV cache: Dev here — short answer: KV cache and ephemeral inference state are pinned to the customer region for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we route inference through region endpoints and caches are kept in-region for requests served in that region. Fallbacks to other model variants in another region only occur if explicitly configured (and would require consent for cross-region processing). We can provide an architectural note showing routing, cache TTLs, and where logs land.

5) Retention & logging controls: We support configurable retention via account settings for logs and prompts. Default retention is 90 days, but for pilot we can set retention to 30 days via account config (no contract addendum needed). For PII handling we support input redaction and post-ingest masking; engineering can enable automatic token redaction on ingestion for selected fields, or we can run a scheduled job to pseudonymize stored prompts.

Next steps:
- I'll ask Legal to prepare the one-paragraph controller/processor statement and confirm the objection workflow for subprocessors.
- Dev will produce a short architecture note (region routing, KV cache behavior, where logs are stored) by EOD Monday.
- I'll set the pilot account retention to 30 days once you confirm which account (trial vs. pilot).

If you'd like, we can sign the DPA as-is for pilot and track the 48-hour breach notice request as a contract negotiable item — or we can amend the DPA now. Which do you prefer?

Best,
Marissa Cole
marissa@redwood.ai
